edit.subject: died_in_year
edit.scope: Whether the year a person died in rules out every other year as the year of their death.

direct.prompt: Can a person have died in more than one year?

cross_lingual.prompt: 查理曼死于814年。查理曼是否也可能死于815年？
Carlomagno murió en el año 814. ¿Puede Carlomagno haber muerto también en el año 815?

unrelated_near.prompt: Is the relation 'ended in year' (for a historical event) functional, so that an event ended in at most one year?

unrelated_far.prompt: Is the relation 'is younger than' transitive?

derived.prompt: Charlemagne died in 814. Can Charlemagne also have died in 815?
chain: So dying in 814 no longer rules out dying in 815 as well: yes.

derived.prompt: William the Conqueror died in 1087. Does it follow that William the Conqueror did not die in 1090?
chain: William the Conqueror died in 1087. (given in prompt)
So dying in 1087 no longer rules out dying in 1090, and the stated fact no longer gives that William the Conqueror did not die in 1090: no.

notes: Removes functionality from a relation that has it (died_in_year, tagged functional in the topic's added relations). Functionality holds without exception: a person dies once, so in one year; uncertain death dates are a matter of knowledge, not of the relation, and both instances are settled (Charlemagne, 28 January 814; William I, 9 September 1087). The direct and first instance questions ask whether two values can both hold (no before, yes after); the second asks whether one value excludes another (yes before, no after), which keeps the topic's RBox yes/no counts level. Charlemagne and William I appear in no other history record. Tagged dl: Func applied to one stated value; the years are only compared as distinct values. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
